summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recent benchmark runs comparing Redwood inference runtime against Novus's baseline provider (CloudServe AI). Discussed latency/throughput deltas, observed p95/p99 regressions under long sequence tails, batching strategies, KV/prefix caching benefits, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed on targeted 95th-percentile stress run, handoff to Dedicated H100 run, and security doc exchange.

transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-19 Time: 13:30 PST Duration: 52m Attendees: John Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Maria Alvarez (CTO, Novus), Kevin Park (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Infra), Laura Chen (Security), Evan (PM)

00:00 John Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking — want to kick off, quick agenda; go over this week's lab runs, surface any regressions vs baseline and agree next steps.
00:12 Maria Alvarez: Yep, thanks John. High level we ran your last config against CloudServe baseline overnight. We saw overall better throughput but some tail latency spikes, want to dig into that.
00:25 Priya Desai: Great — I pulled the run files into the sheet (link in chat: https://drive.google.com/redwood-novus-poc-bench). I can share screen to walk results, but quick TLDR: avg tokens/sec up ~22% vs baseline on same GPU, but p95/p99 for sequences >1k tokens sometimes worse by 10-30%.
00:45 Kevin Park: That matches our observation. For clinical note generation some documents hit 1.2k tokens and that's where CloudServe seemed more stable for p99.
00:58 John Carter: Noted. Priya, can you explain what we changed in the runtime? I remember we enabled continuous batching and prefix caching for this run?
01:06 Priya Desai: Yeah so config A used continuous batching + KV prefix caching + int8 quant profile. The main difference is our runtime aggressively reuses KV cache across similar prompts which helps throughput, but for longer sequences there's more KV eviction churn under our current cache window — that can cause p99 jitter. Also our kernel selection prioritized fused attention kernels that are higher throughput but slightly higher per-step latency on very long seqs.
01:34 Samir Patel: Quick Q — what GPUs were you testing on? We ran both on A100 and H100 instances. Baseline used CloudServe on H100 as well.
01:42 Priya Desai: The parity run was on H100 in your lab; both sides were H100 (same machine type). We also replicated on an A100 and saw similar relative gains on avg throughput but the long-tail discrepancy was smaller on A100.
01:58 Evan (PM): Could the model variant differ? Are we matching the same quant/ops?
02:03 Priya Desai: Model weights were the same base checkpoint. Baseline had a slightly different decoding scheduler and they used a 4-token prefetch which reduced p99. We can replicate that prefetch and compare.
02:20 Marcus Lee: Also we saw a higher retry rate at concurrency spikes (you had 70 concurrent streams). Retries add jitter; was that due to our queue cutoff?
02:31 Priya Desai: Good catch — our queue window currently uses a per-worker batching cutoff tuned for latency-SLOs; at high concurrency it can cause more frequent small batches that interact poorly with cache lifetimes. We have a knob to prefer fewer larger batches when concurrency above threshold which we didn't enable.
02:50 Maria Alvarez: From Novus side the business requirement is p95 < 200ms for short prompts and p95 < 800ms for long docs up to 1.5k. Cost target is 30% below baseline for equivalent quality.
03:07 John Carter: Thanks Maria — that helps. On cost, our initial numbers show 28-33% lower unit costs depending on batching and quantization profile. Priya, did we capture cost deltas in the sheet?
03:17 Priya Desai: Yup — sheet shows token-level cost + infra amortized. Important note: with int8 and prefix caching enabled we see larger savings for workloads with repeated prefixes (very common in templated clinical docs). If the prompts are highly unique, benefit shrinks.
03:34 Kevin Park: Our prompts have a mix — templates for discharge summaries (high reuse) and free text notes (unique). I'll upload the sample set so you can recompute.
03:42 John Carter: Great — Kevin, please drop the set in the shared drive by Monday. That was one of the action items.
03:49 Laura Chen: From security — we need to confirm retention, audit logs, and key management. How do you handle KMS or HSM for Private/Dedicated? Also SOC2 timeframe.
04:01 Priya Desai: For Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations). For hosted we offer envelope encryption and can put logs behind a VPC. I'll share the SOC2 scoping doc and a checklist.
04:14 Laura Chen: Please share the audit logging sample — we need the fields and retention options, also SSO/SAML support.
04:21 John Carter: We'll send a packet after call. Marcus will include the log schema.
04:27 Marcus Lee: Noted. I'll upload an example.
04:32 Kevin Park: Back to perf — Priya you mentioned kernel selection. Can you say what changed between runs? I noticed Redwood's runtime selected a fused attention kernel and CloudServe used a cuBLAS fallback for long seqs.
04:44 Priya Desai: Correct. For seqs under 1024 our fused kernels are faster; above that some kernels have memory growth characteristics that increase per-step latency. We're testing a hybrid kernel selector that chooses the fused kernel for mid sequences and a streaming-friendly kernel for very long sequences.
05:02 John Carter: Sounds like a clear mitigation. Timeline on hybrid selector?
05:06 Priya Desai: We can prototype in 3 business days, but better to run an A/B in the lab — toggle selector for a controlled subset of requests. Would like Kevin to provide traffic shape.
05:18 Kevin Park: I can provide histograms by Monday. Also, when you say 'prefix caching' — can you confirm cache lifetime and eviction policy? Our documents sometimes share prefixes for first 200 tokens but diverge after.
05:31 Priya Desai: Cache lifetime for this run was 30s idle timeout and a sliding window up to 10k tokens; eviction is LRU per worker. That setting may be too aggressive for your long documents where prefix reuse spans multiple requests. We can extend to 5 min for this workload.
05:47 Samir Patel: Extending cache to 5 minutes increases memory usage; do you have numbers for mem overhead?
05:53 Priya Desai: Yes, approx +12% GPU memory footprint for typical KV sizes; we'll add that to the workbook. If memory becomes constrained we can change to a shared cache process to reduce duplication.
06:08 Maria Alvarez: Another datapoint — under a mixed workload of 30% long docs and 70% short prompts, Redwood's token throughput improved but end-to-end user latency for short prompts occasionally spiked when long docs were being processed. Is that expected?
06:23 Priya Desai: That is an artifact of single-queue batching; large requests can delay small batches when scheduling isn't prioritized. We have priority queuing and preemption policies in Dedicated that avoid that, but in hosted default config it can show up. We suggested configuring priority queues per route.
06:39 John Carter: For Novus, given you will likely want dedicated capacity, we recommended setting two queues: fast-path for short prompts with strict latency SLOs and a long-path pool for docs. That reduces interference.
06:53 Kevin Park: If we go dedicated, can you guarantee isolation? We need SLA for p95 and a fallback plan in case of degradation.
06:59 John Carter: Dedicated has capacity isolation and we offer canary + automatic fallback to a compatible, slightly cheaper model variant if the primary overloads. We'll include SLA language in the follow-up.
07:10 Evan (PM): On the baseline side, CloudServe had better p99 on long tails in our runs — is that because they use a prefetch that precomputes attention for initial tokens?
07:20 Priya Desai: They used a decode prefetch and a slightly different KV eviction strategy. We can emulate their prefetch and measure. Prefetch trades some extra compute for lower tail latency.
07:31 Maria Alvarez: Ok let's list the experiments: 1) extend cache lifetime to 5m + re-run concurrency, 2) enable hybrid kernel selector, 3) try prefetch 4-token decode, 4) split queues for fast/long. Agree?
07:44 John Carter: Yes. Priya will own hybrid + cache, Marcus will coordinate the Dedicated run scheduling, John will run cost deltas.
07:52 Priya Desai: Also, small note: quantization profile we used was a conservative int8 with per-channel calibration. We can try mixed float16/int8 hybrid for layers sensitive to numeric stability which might improve p99 on long sequences.
08:07 Kevin Park: That could help maintain quality. We'll also run our evaluation set against golden responses to check for regression.
08:14 Laura Chen: Security question — how are logs surfaced? Can we stream audit logs into our Splunk instance? We need SAML provisioning and an IP allowlist for Dedicated.
08:25 John Carter: Yes — Splunk forwarder support is standard for Dedicated. SAML SSO is available and we can set allowlist IPs on the control plane. Marcus will include sample config.
08:37 Marcus Lee: I'll attach the example in the Drive and follow up via email.
08:44 Maria Alvarez: Any blockers from Redwood side for the next runs?
08:48 Priya Desai: No blockers; need the prompt set and traffic histograms from Novus. Also confirm whether you want us to run the Dedicated H100 pass or prefer we start with Hosted tweaks first.
08:59 Kevin Park: Let's do both in parallel if possible — hosted tweaks first, Dedicated run next week. Samir will confirm infra windows.
09:07 Samir Patel: I should be able to open a maintenance window Dec 29 for Dedicated lab. Will confirm by Monday.
09:13 John Carter: Good. To wrap — recap of deliverables: John share perf workbook now; Priya will push cache + kernel experiment configs and run a hosted pass; Marcus to schedule Dedicated H100 run; Novus to supply prompts and traffic shape; Laura to give SOC2 scope. Expected next sync after hosted pass results or Dec 29 dedicated run.
09:36 Maria Alvarez: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
09:40 John Carter: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite for the Dedicated run and post the artifacts.
09:46 [call ends]
